note: Wednesday A, workplace English（职场英语）: 事 si6 ×3, then BBC 6 Minute English “What English phrases really mean” (~6 min). 3 BBC vocab cards + 1 check-back line are the only new cards. Hard recall: the cue is now ONE keyword (skeleton fading), say each aloud before flipping, sets of 3–4. Then a 30–60 sec “Just to confirm I’ve got this right…” check-back. 加油！

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: say 事 (si6, low flat tone 低平调) three times in a row. Low and flat, not mid like 試 si3.
tasks.script: 事 si6 · 事 si6 · 事 si6 (low, flat, no rise)

tasks.title: BBC 6 Minute English: “What English phrases really mean” (listen ~6 min; notice mare / the done thing / miffed)

tasks.prompt: Workplace output, 30–60 sec: check back a process with “Just to confirm I’ve got this right…”. Point → reason → example. Say it aloud before opening the script.
tasks.script:
Point: Just to confirm I’ve got this right: I draft the update, you review it, and then I send it to the team.
Reason: I would rather check now than fix a mistake later.
Example: So today I will send the draft by noon, you review it tomorrow, and I send the final version on Friday. Is that correct?

questions.explain: 事 si6 is low and flat. 低平调。

questions.q: BBC: if a colleague says “I’ve had a mare of a day”, what do they mean?
questions.explain: mare = nightmare, often a bit of exaggeration. 糟心的一天。

questions.q: “Is that the done thing?” asks about…
questions.explain: the done thing = 约定俗成的做法。

questions.q: “Just to confirm I’ve got this right…” is used to…

questions.explain: 先说重点，再讲原因，最后举例。
